question.prompt:
The area of trapezoid \(ABCD\) is \(164\text{ cm}^2.\) The altitude is \(8\) cm, \(AB\) is \(10\) cm, and \(CD\) is \(17\) cm. What is \(BC,\) in centimeters?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The known height lets us turn the sloping sides into right triangles. Their horizontal sides will tell us how much longer \(AD\) is than \(BC\).

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

Drop perpendiculars from \(B\) and \(C\) to \(AD\), meeting it at \(E\) and \(F\), respectively. Since the bases \(BC\) and \(AD\) are parallel, \(BEFC\) is a rectangle. Thus \(BE=CF=8\) and \(EF=BC\).

The right triangles \(ABE\) and \(CFD\) have hypotenuses \(10\) and \(17\). By the Pythagorean theorem, taking positive roots because these are lengths,
\[
AE=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6,
\qquad FD=\sqrt{17^2-8^2}=15.
\]
In the indicated configuration, \(AD=AE+EF+FD\), so
\[
AD-BC=6+15=21.
\]
The trapezoid area formula also gives
\[
AD+BC=\frac{2\cdot164}{8}=41.
\]
Subtracting the difference from the sum leaves twice the shorter base. Therefore
\[
BC=\frac{41-21}{2}=\boxed{10\text{ cm}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{B}\).
solutions.title: Find the sum and difference of the bases
